The AI label on Samsung Galaxy photos: what it is and what you can remove

Edited a photo with Galaxy AI and now it shows an AI icon, or social networks label it as AI-generated? Samsung adds two different things to those images. Here is what each one is and what you can do about it.

Updated 2026-11-26 · 4 min read
Clean your files in secondsFree, no sign-up, and everything runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
Open IA Cleaner

Two different things: a visible mark and metadata

  • A visible mark in the corner of images changed with generative Galaxy AI features (such as Generative Edit). It is part of the picture itself — pixels, not metadata.
  • Metadata written into the file stating that the image was edited with AI. On recent models this can include C2PA Content Credentials. Gallery, other apps and social networks like Instagram, Facebook or TikTok can read it and show “AI-generated content” labels.

Remove the AI metadata

  1. On your phone, open iacleaner.com → Images in Samsung Internet or Chrome.
  2. Tap the drop zone and choose the photo from your gallery.
  3. The report shows the metadata found and flags AI-related entries; the box What the original reveals lists the tool and AI use.
  4. Tap Download clean image and share that copy.

The photo never leaves your phone and its pixels are not changed.

What IA Cleaner can’t remove

The visible mark is drawn into the image, so removing metadata does not touch it. IA Cleaner does not edit pixels. Also keep in mind that platforms can detect AI in other ways, and many require you to disclose realistic AI edits — be honest where it matters.

Tips

  • Keep the original in your gallery; the clean copy is a separate file.
  • Galaxy AI features that don’t generate new content usually don’t add these labels. If you are unsure, drop the photo into IA Cleaner and check the report.

What IA Cleaner detects and removes

In photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) it identifies and removes GPS location, camera and phone model, dates, editing apps, XMP and IPTC data, C2PA Content Credentials and embedded AI prompts. Pixels and colour profile stay the same. You see the full report first — every block found, with AI-related ones flagged — and then download the clean copy.
